title: What to eat
intro: All three of these are walk-in — no advance booking needed for lunch. Mousel's Cantine gets busy at dinner, so a same-day call helps if arriving in the evening.

items.name: Marché Place Guillaume II
items.how: In the main square, a 5-minute walk from the Palace and Cathedral.
items.why: Regional produce, cheese, roast chicken and a food-stall cluster — the easiest, most casual lunch in the old town, and it lands on this trip's Saturday.

items.name: Mousel's Cantine
items.area: Clausen, at the foot of the Bock
items.how: A 10-minute walk downhill from Bock Casemates — a natural stop after the tunnels.
items.crowd_tip: Lunch generally seats walk-ins; dinner fills up, especially Fri–Sat — call ahead or use the online booking form if arriving after 19:00.
items.why: 200 years in the same Clausen building, serving Judd mat Gaardebounen — smoked pork collar and broad beans, Luxembourg's national dish.

items.name: Oberweis
items.hours: ⚠ Tearoom ≈Mon–Sat 08:00–17:15, shop ≈07:45–18:00, closed Sundays — confirm against the shop before relying on it
items.how: On the main shopping street, a few minutes from the Palace and Cathedral.
items.why: Family-run since 1964 and supplier to the Grand Ducal court since 1999 — a coffee-and-pastry break between old-town sights, not a full meal.
